title: Chess Pairing
description:
You are hosting a chess tournament with 2N people. Exactly X of them are rated players, and the remaining 2N-X are unrated players.
Your job is to distribute the players into N pairs, where every player plays against the person paired up with them.
Since you want the rated players to have an advantage, you want to pair them with unrated players. Thus, you want to minimize the number of rated players whose opponent is also rated.
Print the minimum number of rated players whose opponents are also rated, among all possible pairings.
inputFormat:
The first line of input will contain a single integer T, denoting the number of test cases.
Each test case consists of 1 line containing 2 space-separated integers N and X, meaning there are 2N players, and X of them are rated.
outputFormat: For each test case, output on a new line the minimum number of rated players who will have rated opponents.

title: Battle Fighter
description:
Fighter is on a solo mission in Battleland, facing N enemies. The strength of the i-th enemy is denoted by A_i.
Fighter starts with an initial strength of H and a resistance level of X.

Here are the rules of the fight:
• If an enemy's strength is less than or equal to Fighter's resistance (X), Fighter wins without losing any strength.
• If an enemy's strength exceeds Fighter's resistance, Fighter can still win, but only if his strength is strictly greater than the enemy's. In this case, Fighter's strength decreases by the enemy's strength after the battle.

Your task is to find the minimum resistance value (X) that Fighter needs to defeat all N enemies while ensuring he maintains a positive strength after the last battle.
inputFormat:
The first line of input will contain a single integer T, denoting the number of test cases.
Each test case consists of two lines of input:
• The first line of each test case contains two space-separated integers N and H — the number of enemies and Fighter's initial strength, respectively.
• The next line contains N space-separated integers A_1, A_2, ..., A_N — the strengths of the N enemies.
outputFormat: For each test case, output on a new line, the minimum resistance value (X) that Fighter needs to defeat all N enemies while ensuring he maintains a positive strength after the last battle.
constraints:
1 \le T \le 1000
1 \le N, H, A_i \le 10^6
The sum of N over all test cases won't exceed 10^6.

title: Document Organization
description:
Alexandra has been working in the data analysis department of the "TechCorp Solutions" company for as much as n days. Right now her task is to make a series of reports about the department's metrics for the last n days. We know that the main information in a day report is value ai, the department's performance score on the i-th day. If ai is negative, then the department had below-average performance on the i-th day.

Alexandra should sort the daily reports into binders. Each binder should include data on the department's metrics for several consecutive days. Of course, the information on each of the n days should be exactly in one binder. Thus, Alexandra puts information on the first few days in the first binder. The information on the several following days goes to the second binder, and so on.

It is known that the supervisor reviews one daily report binder per day. If one binder has three or more reports for the days in which the department had below-average performance (ai < 0), she becomes concerned and requires additional explanations.

Therefore, Alexandra wants to prepare the binders so that none of them contains information on three or more days with below-average performance, and the number of binders is minimal.

Write a program that, given sequence ai, will print the minimum number of binders.
inputFormat: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100), n is the number of days. The second line contains a sequence of integers a1, a2, ..., an (|ai| ≤ 100), where ai means the department performance score on the i-th day. It is possible that the department has no days with the negative ai.
outputFormat:
Print an integer k — the required minimum number of binders. In the second line print a sequence of integers b1, b2, ..., bk, where bj is the number of day reports in the j-th binder.

If there are multiple ways to sort the reports into k days, print any of them.

title: Alex and Programming Contests
description:
Alex is a programmer and he likes to take part in Code Clash Challenge rounds. However, his region doesn't have reliable internet connection, so Alex sometimes skips rounds.

Code Clash Challenge has rounds of two types: Advanced (for experienced programmers) and Beginner (for novice programmers). Two rounds, Advanced and Beginner, can go simultaneously, (Advanced round cannot be held without Beginner) in all other cases the rounds don't overlap in time. Each round has a unique identifier — a positive integer. The rounds are sequentially (without gaps) numbered with identifiers by the starting time of the round. The identifiers of rounds that are run simultaneously are different by one, also the identifier of the Advanced round is always greater.

Alex is a novice programmer, so he can take part only in rounds of Beginner type. At the moment he is taking part in a Beginner round, its identifier equals to x. Alex remembers very well that he has taken part in exactly k rounds before this round. Also, he remembers all identifiers of the rounds he has taken part in and all identifiers of the rounds that went simultaneously with them. Alex doesn't remember anything about the rounds he missed.

Alex is wondering: what minimum and what maximum number of Beginner rounds could he have missed? Help him find these two numbers.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers: x (1 ≤ x ≤ 4000) — the round Alex is taking part in today, and k (0 ≤ k < 4000) — the number of rounds he took part in.

Next k lines contain the descriptions of the rounds that Alex took part in before. If Alex took part in one of two simultaneous rounds, the corresponding line looks like: "1 num2 num1" (where num2 is the identifier of this Beginner round, num1 is the identifier of the Advanced round). It is guaranteed that num1 - num2 = 1. If Alex took part in a usual Beginner round, then the corresponding line looks like: "2 num" (where num is the identifier of this Beginner round). It is guaranteed that the identifiers of all given rounds are less than x.
outputFormat: Print in a single line two integers — the minimum and the maximum number of rounds that Alex could have missed.
